entities.name: PMID:29478034
observations: UK guideline on oesophageal dilatation in clinical practice; defines refractory and recurrent benign strictures using dilation response and recurrence intervals.

entities.name: PMID:35477807
observations: Retrospective cohort: weekly dilation in complex benign strictures; 57% of 21 patients who had failed prior dilation at intervals ≥2 weeks achieved long-term success; overall success 83.3% in 36 previously undilated patients.
Reported one perforation and one bleed across 488 dilations.

entities.name: Timing criteria in strictures
observations: Consensus criteria define refractory stricture as inability to reach 14 mm after five dilation sessions at approximately 2-week intervals; recurrent stricture means inability to maintain 14 mm for at least 4 weeks after successful dilation. These are operational definitions, not proof that timing alone causes poor outcomes.

entities.name: Weekly dilation outcomes
observations: In a retrospective cohort of complex benign strictures, weekly dilation rescued long-term success in 57% after failure of prior sessions spaced ≥2 weeks; observational design cannot establish superiority or isolate interval effects.
